questions.q:

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life. This ability of the plants is due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body. The cells of such meristems have the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate.
questions.subject: Botany

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Since increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly, one generally measures some quantity which is more or less proportional to it. Growth is, therefore, measured by a variety of parameters some of which are: increase in fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The cells at shoot apex and root apex is constantly dividing
Reason: These cells represent the meristematic phase of growth and are rich in protoplasm

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The constantly dividing cells, both at the root apex and the shoot apex, represent the meristematic phase of growth. The cells in this region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

Both Assertion and Reason are false

questions.subject: Botany

Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The increased growth per unit time is termed as growth rate. Thus, rate of growth can be expressed mathematically.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Quantitative comparisons between growth of living system can be made in two ways

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Quantitative comparisons between the growth of living system can also be made in two ways : (i) measurement and the comparison of total growth per unit time is called the absolute growth rate. (ii) The growth of the given system per unit time expressed on a common basis, e.g., per unit initial parameter is called the relative growth rate.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth.
Reason: Plant cells require water for growth
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement which in turn requires water. Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth. Thus, plant growth and further development is intimately linked to the water status of the plant.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Deviation in temperature can be detrimental for plants
Reason: Plants require an optimum temperature for its growth
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Every plant organism has an optimum temperature range best suited for its growth. Any deviation from this range could be detrimental to its survival.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The cells derived from root apical and shoot-apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions. This act leading to maturation is termed as differentiation.

questions.q:

Assertion: Formation of meristems – interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells are examples of dedifferentiation
Reason: Meristems are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the ability to divide
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation. For example, formation of meristems – interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Meristems derived from dedifferentiation can undergo redifferentiation
Reason: Differentiation in plants is open
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Formation of meristems occur – interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells(Dedifferentiation). While doing so, such meristems/tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform specific functions, i.e., get redifferentiated.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Differentiation in plants is open
Reason: Cells positioned away from root apical meristems differentiate as root-cap cells, while those pushed to the periphery mature as epidermis.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Differentiation in plants is open, because cells/tissues arising out of the same meristem have different structures at maturity.
questions.subject: Botany

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Growth, differentiation and development are very closely related events in the life of a plant thus development is considered as the sum of growth and differentiation.

questions.solution: The PGRs of the other group play an important role in plant responses to wounds and stresses of biotic and abiotic origin. They are also involved in various growth inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission.

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.

Reason: The PGR abscisic acid belongs to this group of plant growth inhibitors
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin when they observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism). After a series of experiments, it was concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile .
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Gibberelic acid was discovered from a fungal pathogen
Reason: Miller et al.(1955) termed the cytokinesis promoting substance as kinetin
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The ‘bakanae’ (foolish seedling) disease of rice seedlings, was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi. E. Kurosawa (1926) reported the appearance of symptoms of the disease in rice seedlings when they were treated with sterile filtrates of the fungus. The active substances were later identified as gibberellic acid.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Abscisic acid was formerly considered as three different inhibitors
Reason: The PGR abscisic acid is a plant growth inhibitor
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: During mid-1960s, three independent researches reported the purification and chemical characterisation of three different kinds of inhibitors: inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin. Later all the three were proved to be chemically identical. It was named abscisic acid (ABA).
questions.subject: Botany

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: The term ‘auxin’ is applied to the indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), and to other natural and synthetic compounds having certain growth regulating properties, mainly plant growth promoters.
questions.subject: Botany

Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Gibberellins promotes bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: Cytokinins were discovered as kinetins
Reason: Kinetins occur naturally in plants
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: Cytokinins have specific effects on cytokinesis, and were discovered as kinetin (a modified form of adenine, a purine) from the autoclaved herring sperm DNA. Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants.

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

questions.solution: Cytokinin help to produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation thus Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance.

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false

Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false

questions.q:

Assertion: ABA inhibits dormancy in seeds
Reason: ABA helps seeds to germinate faster
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
questions.solution: By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. The first step of plant growth is seed germination
2. Development is the sum of three processes - growth, variation and differentiation
3. The seed germinates when unfavourable conditions for growth exist in the environment.
4. In absence of such favourable conditions the seeds do not germinate and goes into a period of suspended growth or rest.
5. Once unfavourable conditions return, the seeds resume metabolic activities and growth takes place.
questions.solution: The first step in the process of plant growth is seed germination. The seed germinates when favourable conditions for growth exist in the environment. In absence of such favourable conditions the seeds do not germinate and goes into a period of suspended growth or rest. Once favourable conditions return, the seeds resume metabolic activities and growth takes place.

3. Growth can be defined as an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts or even of an individual cell.
4. Growth does not occur at the expense of energy.
questions.solution: Growth can be defined as an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts or even of an individual cell. Generally, growth is accompanied by metabolic processes (both anabolic and catabolic), that occur at the expense of energy. Therefore, for example, expansion of a leaf is growth.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life
2. Meristems have the capacity to divide
3. This form of growth wherein new cells are always being added to the plant body by the activity of the meristem is called the open form of growth.
4. This ability of the plants to grow throughout life is due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body.
5. The products of mersitem division soon lose the capacity to divide and such cells make up the plant body
questions.solution: Plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life. This ability of the plants is due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body. The cells of such meristems have the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate. The product, however, soon loses the capacity to divide and such cells make up the plant body. This form of growth wherein new cells are always being added to the plant body by the activity of the meristem is called the open form of growth.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

2. Ethylene is used to delay flowering
3. Cytokinins reduce chloroplast formation
4. Ethephon can form ethylene

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Lateral meristems appear later in a plants life
2. Meristems are not involed in secondary growth
3. Vascular cambium and cork-cambium appear early in life.
4. These are the meristems that cause the increase in the length of the organs in which they are active.
questions.solution: In dicotyledonous plants and gymnosperms, the lateral meristems, vascular cambium and cork-cambium appear later in life. These are the meristems that cause the increase in the girth of the organs in which they are active.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Zeatin is a form of naturally occuring cytokinin
2. Cytokinins have specific effects on karyokinesis
3. Root apices contain cytokinins
4. It inhibits production new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation.
5. Cytokinins help promote the apical dominance.
questions.solution: Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Natural cytokinins are synthesised in regions where rapid cell division occurs, for example, root apices, developing shoot buds, young fruits etc. It helps to produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation. Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

1. Growth results due to increase in protoplasm
2. Increase in protoplasm can be easily measured directly
3. Growth cannot be measured by a variety of parameters some of
which are: increase in fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number
4. One single maize root apical mersitem can give rise to more than17,500 new cells per hour
5. Cells in a watermelon may increase in size by upto 3,50,000 times.

Sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in their stems. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Growth is measured only by cell number
2. Growth is reversible
3. Increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly
4. Growth in plants is open
questions.solution: Increase in protoplasm is difficult to measure directly, one generally measures some quantity which is more or less proportional to it. Growth is measured by a variety of parameters some of which are: increase in fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume and cell number.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Period of growth is generally divided into two phases
2. Root apex represents maturation phase of growth
3. The cells in this region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei.
4. The cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation.
5. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase.
questions.solution: The period of growth is generally divided into three phases, namely, meristematic, elongation and maturation. The constantly dividing cells, both at the root apex and the shoot apex, represent the meristematic phase of growth. The cells in this region are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei. The cells proximal (just next, away from the tip) to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Ethylene is synthesized by tissues undergoing senescence
2. Cytokinins promote apical shoot growth
3. Ethylene promotes dormancy in seeds
4. Fruit ripening is enhanced by ethylene
questions.solution: Ethylene is a simple gaseous PGR. It is synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and ripening fruits. Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during ripening of the fruits.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Differentiation occurs in root apical and shoot apical meristems
2. Cells lose their protoplasm to form tracheary element
3. The dead differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions.
4. Interfascicular cambium and cork cambium form from fully redifferentiated parenchyma cells.
questions.solution: The cells derived from root apical and shoot-apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions. This act leading to maturation is termed as differentiation. During differentiation, cells undergo few to major structural changes both in their cell walls and protoplasm. For example, to form a tracheary element, the cells would lose their protoplasm.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. The cells proximal to the meristematic zone represents the phase of maturation
2. Cells in the meristematic phase of growth are devoid of protoplasm
3. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in the elongation phase.
4. Further away from the apex, i.e., more proximal to the phase of elongation, lies the portion of axis which is undergoing the phase of maturation.
5. The cells of this zone, attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.
questions.solution: The cells proximal to the meristematic zone represent the phase of elongation. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in this phase. . Further away from the apex, i.e., more proximal to the phase of elongation, lies the portion of axis which is undergoing the phase of maturation. The cells of this zone, attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Apical dominance prevents lateral buds from growing
2. Auxins inhibit parthenocarpy
3. 2,4-D is used to kill monocotyledonous plants
4. Auxin also controls xylem differentiation and helps in cell division.
questions.solution: In most higher plants, the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of the lateral (axillary) buds, a phenomenon called apical dominance. Auxin also controls xylem differentiation and helps in cell division.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Stationary phase is a phase marked by increased division of cells
2. Root elongation at constant rate is an example of arithmetic growth
3. In geometric growth the initial growth is slow (lag phase), and it increases rapidly thereafter – at a logarithmic rate (log or exponential phase).
4. Both the progeny cells following mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide and continue to do so.
5. With limited nutrient supply, the growth slows down leading to a stationary phase.
questions.solution: The simplest expression of arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate. Let us now see what happens in geometrical growth. In most systems, the initial growth is slow (lag phase), and it increases rapidly thereafter – at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase). Here, both the progeny cells following mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide and continue to do so. However, with limited nutrient supply, the growth slows down leading to a stationary phase

3. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition are the characteristics of the cells in the elongation phase.
4. The cells in the meristematic phase are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei.
questions.solution: Away from the apex, i.e., more proximal to the phase of elongation, lies the portion of axis which is undergoing the phase of maturation. The cells of this zone, attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications.

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. The plant cells grow in size due to mitosis
2. Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth
3. Plant growth and further development is not linked to the water status of the plant
4. Water also provides the medium for enzymatic activities needed for growth.
5. Oxygen helps in releasing metabolic energy essential for growth activities.
questions.solution: The plant cells grow in size by cell enlargement which in turn requires water. Turgidity of cells helps in extension growth. Thus, plant growth and further development is intimately linked to the water status of the plant.

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to environment
2. Development is considered as the sum of growth, differentiation and variation
3. Difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup represent the heterophyllous development due to environment
4. The phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.
questions.solution: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, leaves of the juvenile plant are different in shape from those in mature plants. On the other hand, difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment (Figure 13.9). This phenomenon of heterophylly is an example of plasticity.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. The plant growth regulators are large, complex moleculres
2. All PGRs promote plant growth
3. The PGRs of the other group play an important role in plant responses to wounds and stresses of biotic and abiotic origin.
4. They are also involved in various growth inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission.
5. Plant growth regulators are variously described as plant growth substances, plant hormones or phytohormones
questions.solution: The plant growth regulators (PGRs) are small, simple molecules of diverse chemical composition. Plant growth regulators are variously described as plant growth substances, plant hormones or phytohormones. The PGRs of the other group play an important role in plant responses to wounds and stresses of biotic and abiotic origin. They are also involved in various growth inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. Dedifferentiation renables cells to divide that have lost the capacity to divide
2. Formation of meristems from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of dedifferentiation
3. While dedifferentiating, such meristems/tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform specific functions, i.e., get redifferentiated.
4. Formation of meristems – interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells.
questions.solution: The living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation. For example, formation of meristems – interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells. While doing so, such meristems/tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform specific functions, i.e., get redifferentiated.

questions.solution: Cytokinin helps to produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation. Cytokinins help overcome the apical dominance.

Read the following statements and choose the following option:
1. All the changes in a plants life from germination to senescence is termed as development
2. Heterophylly in larkspur is an example of plasticity
3. Difference in shapes of leaves produced in air and those produced in water in buttercup also represent the heterophyllous development due to environment
4. Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases
of life to form different kinds of structures.
questions.solution: Development is a term that includes all changes that an organism goes through during its life cycle from germination of the seed to senescence.Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called plasticity, e.g., heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur.

2. H.H cousins confirmed the release of ethylene from ripened oranges
3. Three researches coordinated and reported the purification and chemical characterisation of three different kinds of inhibitors: inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin.

5. inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin-all the three were proved to be chemically different.
questions.solution: The ‘bakanae’ (foolish seedling) disease of rice seedlings, was caused by a fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi. H.H. Cousins (1910) confirmed the release of a volatile substance from ripened oranges that hastened the ripening of stored unripened bananas. Later this volatile substance was identified as ethylene, a gaseous PGR.

questions.q:
Growth Parameters in PlantsDescription
A. Fresh Weight1. A parameter to measure growth proportional to the increase in protoplasm.
B. Cell Number2. Used to express growth in tissues where cell division is significant.
C. Cell Size3. Measurement that expresses growth in cells where expansion is significant.
D. Surface Area4. Used to measure growth in structures like dorsiventral leaves.
questions.solution:
A - 4: Fresh weight is a parameter used to measure growth, proportional to the increase in protoplasm.
B - 2: Cell number is used to express growth in tissues with significant cell division, like the maize root apical meristem.
C - 3: Cell size expresses growth in cases where cells expand significantly, such as in watermelon cells.
D - 1: Surface area is used to measure growth in dorsiventral leaves.

Terms Related to Plant Growth and DevelopmentDescriptions
A. Differentiation1. The process where living differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide.
B. Dedifferentiation2. Cells derived from meristems mature to perform specific functions.
C. Redifferentiation3. The process where cells that regained the capacity to divide again lose this ability and mature.
D. Lignocellulosic Walls4. Structural change in cells to support water conduction under tension.
questions.solution:
A - 2: Differentiation is when cells derived from meristems mature to perform specific functions.
B - 1: Dedifferentiation is the process where living differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide.
C - 3: Redifferentiation is when cells that regained the capacity to divide again lose this ability and mature to perform specific functions.

questions.q:

B. Interfascicular Cambium2. Maturation involving loss of protoplasm and development of strong secondary walls.

D. Loss of Division Capacity4. Cells perform specific functions after maturing from a dividing state.
questions.solution:
A - 2: Tracheary elements form by differentiation, involving loss of protoplasm and development of lignocellulosic walls.
B - 1: Interfascicular cambium is formed by dedifferentiation from fully differentiated cells.
C - 3: Cork cambium is another example of dedifferentiation from parenchyma cells.
D - 4: After dedifferentiation, cells that lose their capacity to divide and mature are examples of redifferentiation.

B. Geometric growth2. Rapid exponential growth phase in the sigmoid curve.

D - 2: The log phase is the rapid exponential growth phase in the sigmoid curve.
E - 5: The stationary phase occurs when growth slows down due to limitations like nutrient depletion.
